title: Knowledge of others' minds (3.19)
hook: samyama on another person's state of mind reveals that mind, and the very next sutra draws a line around what it can't see

segments.voice: Yesterday: knowledge of past and future, and your line, the powers begin. See how a thing changes, all the way, and time opens both ways. Day four hundred sixty-nine, the end of a week.

Your phone buzzes. It's your oldest friend. One word: hey. No punctuation. And somehow you already know something's wrong. Not what. Just that. You've read a thousand of their heys, and this one is different. You text back: what happened? Nobody calls that a superpower. It's what close attention to one person, for years, starts to do. Today Patanjali names a power that sounds like a much bigger version of that. And then, immediately, he tells you exactly where it stops.
screen: `ONE WORD: HEY.` → `SOMETHING'S WRONG.` → `NOT WHAT. JUST THAT.`

segments.voice: Sutra 3.19: by samyama on the idea in another's mind, knowledge of that other mind. The word is pratyaya, the content of awareness at a given moment, the mood or idea running through it. Rest concentration, meditation and absorption on that, and the other person's state of mind becomes clear: troubled, calm, grasping, glad. Then comes the warning, in the very next line. Sutra 3.20: but not its object. You can know that the mind is angry, but not what it's angry at, because that wasn't the object of the samyama. The classical commentary is careful here. The power reaches the color of the mind, not its whole story. That's honest, and a little humbling. Even at its height, knowing another person has a limit, and the sutra writes the limit right into the power. It's worth sitting with the order of the book, too. Patanjali didn't open with powers. He opened with non-harm, truth, not stealing. Anyone who reads a mind is standing very close to someone else's inner life, and the first limb has already said how to stand there. Now the week, looked at from the top. Pranayama, the veil thins. Pratyahara, the senses follow the mind home. Concentration, meditation, absorption. The three together, samyama. The transformations, what changes. Past and future. And today, other minds, with a line drawn around them. A week that went inward, and now begins to turn outward again, toward what that inward work can do.
screen: `PRATYAYA: WHAT'S IN A MIND NOW.` · `KNOW THE MIND, NOT ITS OBJECT.` · `THE LIMIT IS WRITTEN IN.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `AND THE WARNING.`

segments.voice: Today's practice reads the closest mind there is, your own. Sit steady and easy, and rest on the breath. Then ask: what's the color of my mind right now? Restless, tired, glad, worried. Name it in one word. Don't chase the reasons behind it. Just the color. Breathe with it. Then, if you like, bring to mind someone you love, and wish their mind well, whatever color it is today. The bell holds the time.
Knowledge of others' minds. By samyama on another's state of mind, that mind is known, though not what it's fixed on.
Your line: and the warning. Today, when you sense someone's mood, let that be enough. Ask, don't assume the reason. Day four hundred sixty-nine.

screen: `DAY 469 COUNTS.` → `A WEEK OF THE INNER LIMBS, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: INVISIBILITY; STRENGTH; THE ELEPHANT.`

howItsDone: Many Hindu stories describe sages who know the minds of those who come to them, and teachers of the Yoga Sutras point to 3.20's limit and to the yamas as the frame in which any such power is held.

myth: 3.19 says the yogi reads every detail of another's thoughts
3.20 says not its object: the state of the mind, not what it's about.
the limit is stated in the very next sutra
the Yoga Sutras open with powers and add ethics later
the first limb, the yamas, came long before; the powers appear in book three.

fork.setup: you sense a friend's mind is angry. by sutra 3.20, what can you know?
options: that the mind is angry, but not at what.
exactly who they're angry at, and why.
fork.reveal: 3.20: but not its object, since that wasn't the object of the samyama. the power reaches the color of the mind, not its whole story.

original.note: Sanskrit para-citta-jñāna: knowledge (jñāna) of another's (para) mind (citta), 3.19.

trapdoor: what you thought: yogis claim to read minds.
what it means: samyama on another's state of mind reveals that state, but not what the mind is fixed on.
what a scholar hears: pratyayasya para-citta-jnanam (3.19); na ca tat salambanam (3.20), the support or object not included; numbering of these sutras varies by edition.

notes: Week end (days 463–469): look-back included in the teach.
'And the warning' is read here as the limit in 3.20; the larger warning about the powers (3.37) comes on day 473 and is only hinted at.
The link to the yamas is the script's reflection on the book's order, not a claim made in 3.19–3.20.
Some editions number 3.19–3.20 differently (e.g. 3.18–3.19); confirm against the outline's edition.
